tools.name: Joplin
tools.description: Note-taking app that syncs across phone and laptop and keeps your notes private.
tools.safetyNote: End-to-end encryption must be enabled manually for sync. Keep the encryption password safe: it cannot be recovered. Enable it on one device first, then sync the others rather than setting it up separately on every device.

guide.title: How to install Joplin
requirements: A Windows or macOS computer. Joplin has a separate download for each.

steps.text: There is nothing else to install first. The Joplin installer is all you need.
Open Joplin's official install page.
Find the Windows download and click the installer. Its file name starts with Joplin-Setup and ends in .exe.
steps.screenshot: the Windows download on Joplin's install page

steps.text: Open the downloaded file and follow the steps on screen.
Open Joplin's official install page.
Find the macOS downloads. There are two .dmg files.
steps.screenshot: the macOS downloads on Joplin's install page

steps.text: If your Mac has an Apple Silicon (M1) chip, download the file with arm64 in its name.
If your Mac does not have that chip, download the other .dmg file.
Open the downloaded file and follow the steps on screen.
Please follow Joplin's official Linux instructions on its install page.

tools.name: SiYuan
tools.description: Note-taking app where you link ideas together and keep everything on your own device.
tools.safetyNote: Do not sync the live workspace using a normal third-party sync folder: the developers warn this can corrupt data. Keep the workspace outside the installation directory to avoid losing it during updates. If self-hosting, configure strong access authentication.
tools.caution: Worth keeping for advanced linked notes, but follow its workspace/sync rules and check paid-feature requirements before relying on it across devices.

tools.name: Marp
tools.description: Lets you write slides in plain text (Markdown) and turn them into a slideshow.
tools.safetyNote: Review exports; avoid untrusted embedded HTML/scripts.
tools.replaces: PowerPoint / Canva Pro, for basic presentations

guide.title: How to install Marp CLI
requirements: "Node.js v18 and later is required to use Marp CLI." (Marp CLI official docs)
Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge or Mozilla Firefox, if you want to make a PDF.
A terminal: PowerShell on Windows, or Terminal on macOS and Linux.

steps.text: Open the official Node.js download page.
In the section for a prebuilt Node.js, choose Windows, then click Windows Installer (.msi).
steps.screenshot: the Windows Installer button on the Node.js page

steps.text: Open the downloaded file and follow the steps on screen.
This command shows your Node.js version, which must be v18 or later. Open a new PowerShell window and run it there.
This command shows your npm version, so you know npm installed too. Run it in the same PowerShell window.
Open the official Node.js download page.
In the section for a prebuilt Node.js, choose macOS, then click macOS Installer (.pkg).

steps.text: Open the downloaded file and follow the steps on screen.

steps.text: This command shows your Node.js version, which must be v18 or later. Open a new Terminal window and run it there.
This command shows your npm version, so you know npm installed too. Run it in the same Terminal window.
Choose Linux on the official Node.js download page and follow the steps there.
Open your terminal: PowerShell on Windows, or Terminal on macOS and Linux.
This command installs Marp CLI so you can use the marp command in any folder. Type it in your terminal and press Enter.
In a folder of your choice, create a plain-text file named slide-deck.md and write some Markdown in it.
In your terminal, go to that folder: type cd and a space, drag the folder into the terminal window, then press Enter.
This command turns slide-deck.md into slide-deck.html in the same folder. Run it in your terminal, inside that folder.
This command makes a PDF of your slides, using one of the browsers listed under Requirements. Run it in the same place.

tools.name: Jan
tools.description: Desktop app for downloading and chatting with AI models that can run fully offline.
tools.safetyNote: Local models need sufficient RAM; cloud mode sends prompts externally.

tools.name: Zotero
tools.description: Collects, organises, annotates and cites your research sources and PDFs.
tools.safetyNote: Check imported authors, titles and dates before submitting citations.
